tasks.title: Lecture #37
tasks.instruction: Listen to a talk in an economics class.
tasks.transcript: Imagine that you have a full time job, but you want to take a year off to go back to school. What is it going to cost you? Of course there's the cost of tuition for your classes, plus living expenses. But what about the money you're no longer earning at your job because you're now a student? We call that the opportunity cost. Opportunity cost refers to the value of the next best alternative that must be given up when making a choice. It's a fundamental principle in economics that helps individuals and businesses understand the true cost of their decisions. My exercise in imagination illustrates a personal decision, but businesses also face opportunity costs in their operations. For instance, a company may choose to invest in new equipment rather than spend money to expand its product line. The opportunity cost of this decision is the potential revenue that could have been generated from the new products. Understanding opportunity cost helps individuals as well as businesses make informed decisions that maximize their benefits and minimize their losses. It's important to note that opportunity cost is not always measured in financial terms. It can also be related to factors like time, convenience or personal satisfaction. For that reason, opportunity cost can be difficult to quantify, especially when dealing with non monetary factors. Have you ever had to make a decision that included an opportunity cost? Take a few minutes now to think and then I'll ask for volunteers to share.

questions.stem: Why does the speaker ask listeners to imagine a situation at the start of the talk?

options.A: To help explain a potentially unfamiliar concept
options.B: To encourage listeners to take her perspective
options.C: To describe a situation she has experienced
options.D: To compare two different methods for making a decision

questions.analysis: 答案: A 题目问的是: 演讲者在讲座开始时让听众设想一种情境的原因是什么？ 定位原文: “But what about the money you're no longer earning at your job because you're now a student? We call that the opportunity cost.” 选项分析: A. “To help explain a potentially unfamiliar concept.”（帮助解释一个可能不熟悉的概念。）设想情境有助于理解“机会成本”这一概念，因此A选项正确。 B. “To encourage listeners to take her perspective.”（鼓励听众站在她的角度看问题。）虽然设想情境可能帮助听众更好地理解，但目的是为了解释机会成本，因此B选项错误。 C. “To describe a situation she has experienced.”（描述她曾经经历过的情境。）她并未提到自己的亲身经历，因此C选项错误。 D. “To compare two different methods for making a decision.”（比较两种不同的决策方法。）并没有进行这种比较，因此D选项错误。

questions.stem: Why does the speaker talk about investing in new equipment?

options.A: To suggest that not all business decisions include an opportunity cost
options.B: To provide an example of a decision made by most businesses
options.C: To illustrate how businesses take opportunity cost into consideration
options.D: To highlight the importance of weighing all options before investing

questions.analysis: 答案: C 题目问的是: 为什么演讲者谈到投资新设备？ 定位原文: “but businesses also face opportunity costs in their operations. For instance, a company may choose to invest in new equipment rather than spend money to expand its product line. The opportunity cost of this decision is the potential revenue that could have been generated from the new products.” 选项分析: A. “To suggest that not all business decisions include an opportunity cost.”（建议并非所有商业决策都有机会成本。）并没有这个意思，因此A选项错误。 B. “To provide an example of a decision made by most businesses.”（提供一个大多数企业都会做的决策示例。）这只是一个例子，而不是普遍的决策，因此B选项错误。 C. “To illustrate how businesses take opportunity cost into consideration.”（说明企业如何考虑机会成本。）这个例子明确是为了说明机会成本的概念，因此C选项正确。 D. “To highlight the importance of weighing all options before investing.”（强调在投资前权衡所有选项的重要性。）并没有强调这一点，因此D选项错误。

questions.stem: What does the speaker identify as a challenge related to identifying opportunity costs?

options.C: Choosing which factors to consider in making a decision
options.D: Deciding whether to borrow money to cover the costs

questions.analysis: 答案: A 题目问的是: 演讲者指出识别机会成本时的挑战是什么？ 定位原文: “It's important to note that opportunity cost is not always measured in financial terms. It can also be related to factors like time, convenience or personal satisfaction. For that reason, opportunity cost can be difficult to quantify, especially when dealing with non-monetary factors.” 选项分析: A. “Calculating non-monetary costs.”（计算非货币成本。）演讲者明确指出，机会成本可能包括时间、便利性或个人满意度等非货币因素，这使得计算机会成本更加困难，因此A选项正确。 B. “Comparing unrelated activities.”（比较不相关的活动。）原文并没有提到这个问题，因此B选项错误。 C. “Choosing which factors to consider in making a decision.”（选择在决策中考虑哪些因素。）虽然这是决策过程的一部分，但并未作为挑战特别提到，因此C选项错误。 D. “Deciding whether to borrow money to cover the costs.”（决定是否借钱来支付成本。）没有提到借钱的问题，因此D选项错误。

questions.stem: What does the speaker ask listeners to doat the end of the talk?

options.A: Create their own definition of opportunity cost
options.B: Reflect on their own decision-making experiences
options.C: Break up into small groups for discussion
options.D: Share any experiences they have had making investments

questions.analysis: 答案: B 题目问的是: 演讲者在讲座结束时要求听众做什么？ 定位原文: “Have you ever had to make a decision that included an opportunity cost? Take a few minutes now to think and then I'll ask for volunteers to share.” 选项分析: A. “Create their own definition of opportunity cost.”（创建他们自己的机会成本定义。）演讲者并没有要求听众创建定义，因此A选项错误。 B. “Reflect on their own decision-making experiences.”（反思他们自己的决策经验。）她要求听众思考自己的决策经历，因此B选项正确。 C. “Break up into small groups for discussion.”（分成小组讨论。）并没有提到小组讨论，因此C选项错误。 D. “Share any experiences they have had making investments.”（分享他们做投资时的经验。）她要求分享的是关于决策的经历，而不是投资经历，因此D选项错误。
